name: VHS Cassette
description: A 1:1 VHS video cassette in real LEGO, 184 x 102 x 26 mm: an inner chassis with the tape run, lamp tube and reel spindles inside a shell with two big clear windows; the full-length dust flap swings up and both reels turn.
notice: VHS is a trademark of JVC KENWOOD Corporation.

steps.caption: Chassis, bottom layer: the Technic plates' middle holes are the reel drive holes and the lamp hole; silver screw heads sit flush underneath
The lamp tube: a black 2 x 2 round brick over the lamp hole
Ledges the window hangers land on
White tape guide rollers at the front corners, a white guide post and the posts the top shell's flap pivots land on
The tape run: a black 1 x N plate stood on its edge
Black tiles on it: the tape stretched across the front
The chassis
Lower flange: a white 8 x 8 round plate with a hole in the middle
A full pack of tape: a black 8 x 8 round plate
The hub: a round plate with an axle hole, and a flat white ring round it
Tape wound round the hub
Clear upper flange
The red spindle: push the axle up through the hub
Drop the full supply reel onto the right-hand bearing: its red axle goes down through the round holes
Lower flange: a white 8 x 8 round plate with a hole in the middle
Nearly empty: a second white plate, so the flange shows round a thin pack
The hub: a round plate with an axle hole, and a flat white ring round it
Just a few turns of tape left on the hub
Clear upper flange
The red spindle: push the axle up through the hub
The nearly empty take-up reel on the left-hand bearing
End walls
Top shell, built upside down: the grip-band grilles and the black rims go face down, then plates on them
A third layer, with the flap's pivot blocks (plates with a pin hole)
The face label: black plates running front to back ...
The face label panel: it ties the front and back grip bands together
Bricks with side studs for the spine label
Spine label: plates stood on edge
White tiles: the spine label; black tiles at the ends
The write-protect tab: a tile you can pull off to protect your recording
A window: a 2 x 6 plate stood on its edge, studs to the front
Door frame 1 x 6 x 6, laid flat and pushed onto the plate's top row
The glass
A tile caps the frame's front studs
Six hangers on the plate's back row
The window, hung on its six hangers
Lower the top shell onto the chassis
Dust flap, built flat: plates for the two lower rows
A 1 x 3 plate at each end reaches the top row
2 x N tiles: their top halves hang over the plates and make the flap's top row
Bottom row of tiles
Turn it over: Technic bricks at the ends are the flap's cheeks
Hold the dust flap in place and push a pin through each cheek
